rounds.text: Available Finance Ltd is currently trading at a significant valuation discount compared to its sector, evidenced by a P/B ratio of 0.11x against a sector benchmark of 1.35x [E7]. This deep discount is further supported by a P/E ratio of 1.29x, which stands in stark contrast to the sector benchmark of 20.02x [E6]. Recent operational momentum suggests a positive shift, as evidenced by a 14% YoY increase in sales [E64] and a sequential increase in sales on a quarter-over-quarter basis [E66]. This performance is beginning to translate into market outperformance, with profit growth exceeding 1-year price growth by 13% [E56]. Conceded: the company faces long-term growth challenges, including a 10-year compounded sales growth of -16% [E14], a 5-year compounded sales growth of 2% [E15], and a 3-year compounded sales growth of -1% [E16]. Despite these historical headwinds, the current valuation metrics suggest the market has priced in extreme pessimism that may not reflect the company's recent ability to grow sales by 5% over the trailing twelve months [E17].

Available Finance Ltd is priced at an extreme valuation of 673x earnings based on filed statements [E1]. This lofty price is further compounded by a price-to-book ratio of 7.88x, with the stock trading at ₹ 145 against a book value of just ₹ 18.4 [E2]. Furthermore, investors receive no cash return from their holding, as evidenced by a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4]. Beneath this heavy valuation lies a fundamentally stagnant business engine, demonstrated by a dismal compounded sales growth of -16% over 10 years and -1% over 3 years [E14, E16]. This sluggish top-line performance lags severely behind the sector median sales growth of 16.5% [E76]. Conceded: the company boasts short-term momentum signals including a 5% TTM sales growth and a screen reason noting sales up QoQ [E17, E66].

Conceded: filed statements report a P/E of 673x, a price-to-book ratio of 7.88x at ₹ 145 against a book value of ₹ 18.4, and a 0.00% dividend yield [E1, E2, E4]. However, key-ratios from the data provider completely refute this perceived overvaluation by establishing a starkly low P/E of 1.29x against a sector benchmark of 20.02x, alongside an ultra-cheap P/B of 0.11x versus a sector benchmark of 1.35x [E6, E7]. While long-term historical sales growth shows a 10-year contraction of -16% and a 3-year decline of -1% [E14, E16], the business is actively inflecting upward with positive trailing twelve-month sales growth of 5% [E17] and recent year-over-year sales expansion accelerating to 14% [E64]. This operational turnaround is further validated by the scanX signal engine, which notes sales up quarter-over-quarter [E66] and confirms that profit growth currently exceeds 1-year price growth by 13% as the company begins to outperform expectations [E56].

The bull’s reliance on the 1.29x P/E and 0.11x P/B ratios [E6, E7] is fundamentally undermined by the filed statements, which explicitly report a P/E of 673x and a P/B of 7.88x [E1, E2]. Conceded: the company has shown recent sales growth of 14% YoY and QoQ [E64, E66], yet this short-term activity fails to mask the long-term structural decay evidenced by a 10-year compounded sales growth of -16% and a 3-year decline of -1% [E14, E16]. While the bull highlights an ROA of 0.02% [E8], this figure is abysmal compared to the 1.8% sector benchmark, indicating that the company is failing to generate meaningful returns on its assets despite the claimed operational turnaround [E8]. Furthermore, the lack of any dividend yield [E4] provides no income cushion for investors holding a stock that has struggled to maintain consistent growth over the last decade [E14, E15, E16]. The claim of outperforming expectations [E56] remains speculative when measured against the reality of a 5-year sales growth rate of only 1.76% to 2% [E15, E61], which significantly lags the sector median growth of 16.5% [E76].
